rationale: Extended the store-failure probe to the other request shape a leader can send to a peer whose nextIndex still points past the deleted suffix, and asked for a fresh execution of the revision. The earlier receipt covered the leader that has already walked back to the start of its log and is refused; the added phase sends the append a leader sends while nextIndex is still one past the follower's stale last index - previous index 3 with a new entry 4 - so the receipt now also shows what happens before any walk. A local construction run compiled and showed the intended contrast, but only the controller's clean-copy execution counts, so the request is submitted with the revision reason and no result is claimed here.

scope.description: Observe what the follower does when a leader whose nextIndex still points past a deleted suffix appends the next entry, alongside the whole-log request, against a control that never failed its store.

experiment.prefix: Two cases, each building one real raft node (local id assurance-B) over an in-memory log store wrapped by a store whose StoreLogs returns an injected error once when armed, an in-memory stable store and snapshot store, a second in-memory transport registered as assurance-A connected to the node's transport, and two-second heartbeat, election and lease timeouts. Each case sends four AppendEntries RPCs through that transport into the node's own handler: entries 1-3 at term 1 with previous index 0; entries 2-3 at term 2 with previous index 1, which conflicts at index 2 and makes the handler delete its suffix before storing, with the failure armed only in the first case; entries 1-3 again at term 2 with previous index 0; and finally a single entry 4 at term 2 with previous index 3 and previous term 1, which is what a leader sends while its nextIndex for this peer is one past the follower's stale last index. Each phase logs the response fields, the node's in-memory last index, the wrapped store's last index and which of indices 2 and 4 the store holds. The RPCs are supplied by the test rather than by a live leader; the supplied premise is that these are the request shapes the leader's own builder produces at those nextIndex values.
experiment.revision_reason: The earlier revision measured only the repair shape - the whole-log append a leader sends once its rejections have walked nextIndex back to one - and left out the append a leader sends before any walk, while its nextIndex is still one past the follower's stale last index. This revision adds that fourth phase with its own event and the store's contents at indices 2 and 4, so the receipt shows both request shapes and what the refused and accepted ones leave in the store. Cases, node construction, timeouts and the injected failure are unchanged.
